=== UFC 3-501-01 p.37 ===
UFC 3-501-01 
27 November 2024 
 
 
25 
 
General Voltage Drop Mitigation Strategies and Impacts. 
Voltage drop can be mitigated through various strategies, including increasing 
conductor size, reducing the circuit’s load, decreasing the conductor’s length, 
decreasing conductor temperature, and improving power factor.  When establishing 
distribution equipment placement within a facility, locate panelboards relatively central 
to the loads supplied to minimize circuit lengths.  Likewise, routing the majority of the 
distribution at 480/277V and stepping down to 208/120V more locally to the loads 
served will yield a lower voltage drop to the end devices; this strategy needs to evaluate 
a balance between transformer and circuit costs, as well as requirements to submeter 
different load types when applicable. 
Note increased conductor sizes will yield lower conductor resistances, lead to increased 
fault current values, and impact arc flash values at the equipment buses, potentially 
leading to protection coordination issues.  Designers must ensure all conductor sizes 
are established prior to performing final fault current and arc flash calculations, and 
update safety calculations when modifying existing systems. 
 
Voltage Drop Relationship with Utilization Voltage. 
Voltage drop calculations focus on energy loss through conductors, and voltage drop 
contributes to utilization voltage for end users.  However, voltage drop and utilization 
voltage, which is the actual voltage seen at end-use devices and equipment, are not 
synonymous.  Devices and equipment have acceptable utilization voltage ranges within 
which operation can occur, the lower bound of which can be of a lower voltage than 
yielded by the maximum permitted voltage drop alone.  Other system losses occur 
throughout the distribution system, most notably through transformers, and the voltage 
delivered by the utility service may deviate from the nominal voltage assumed in 
calculations.  Transformer tap settings aid in providing appropriate downstream 
utilization voltage, however, the use of transformer taps does not negate energy losses 
incurred through conductor impedance voltage drop. 
Design and construction personnel must remain cognizant of the utilization voltage 
requirements for the equipment and appliances served.  Adjustments to the distribution 
system, such as the use of transformer taps and/or an increase in conductor sizes, must 
be performed accordingly to ensure proper utilization voltage is provided to the end use 
devices while simultaneously satisfying the voltage drop energy conservation 
requirements. 
Practices used to boost utilization voltage at the load must not be used as a method to 
comply with voltage drop requirements. 
 
Calculation Assumptions and Procedures. 
3-2.7.4.1 
Initial Voltage. 
The use of service transformer taps must not be assumed to compensate for voltage 
drop on the service-entrance equipment side of the calculation start point.  Calculations 

=== UFC 3-501-01 p.38 ===
UFC 3-501-01 
27 November 2024 
 
 
26 
must assume the nominal system voltage (i.e., 208V, 240V, 480V) is present at the 
location described for the calculation starting point. 
3-2.7.4.2 
Starting Point. 
Voltage drop calculations must start at the point of government ownership (i.e., 
transformer, disconnect switch, meter cabinet, or similar).  Where the government owns 
the exterior distribution upstream of the service transformer, the calculation must start at 
the service transformer secondary lugs.  Where the facility is without a service 
transformer and supplied by independent generator or energy storage system, the 
calculation must start at such power supply’s output terminals. 
3-2.7.4.3 
Load Estimations. 
3-2.7.4.3.1 
Capacity. 
The capacity must be 100% of a circuit breaker or fuse device’s nominal rating (e.g., 
100A standard (80%) devices and 100A continuous (100%) devices are both 
considered 100A capacity) for voltage drop calculation purposes.  See UFC 3-520-01 
regarding Adjustable-Trip Devices. 
3-2.7.4.3.2 
Feeder Loads. 
Size feeders to accommodate the maximum permitted load based on the circuit 
ampacity.  Exceptions to this are as follows: 
a. 
Transformer Feeders.  Per ANSI C57.96, transformers complying with 
the ANSI standard are designed for continuous operation at the specified 
temperature rise for normal life expectancy at the rated kVA.  The rated 
kVA may be different than the nameplate or nominal kVA value based 
upon insulation temperature rating, ambient temperature, altitude, and 
other operating conditions. 
For voltage drop purposes, a transformer’s secondary feeders must 
assume a load equivalent to the transformer’s nominal output rating. 
For voltage drop purposes, a transformer’s primary feeders must assume 
the same load as identified above for the secondary feeders PLUS 6% 
transformer loss load. 
b. 
Motor Feeders.  Motor overcurrent protection is located at the overloads 
and NFPA 70 categorizes the circuits from the circuit breakers to the 
overcurrent protection as feeders.  As on transformer primary circuits, 
circuit breakers are sized to account for inrush.  Utilize the circuit’s total 
full-load amps (FLA) based on NFPA 70 Article 430 tables for voltage drop 
calculations.  Additionally, this circuit must be considered a “branch circuit” 
for voltage drop compliance purposes only. 

=== UFC 3-501-01 p.39 ===
UFC 3-501-01 
27 November 2024 
 
 
27 
Fire pumps must comply with the voltage drop requirements identified in 
NFPA 70 Article 695 in lieu of the limits stated in this section. 
c. 
Air-Conditioning and Refrigerating Equipment Feeders.  The voltage 
drop load must be the rated-load current or full-load current marked on the 
nameplate as identified in NFPA 70 Article 440.  Additionally, this circuit 
must be considered a “branch circuit” for voltage drop compliance 
purposes only. 
d. 
Variable Frequency Drives/Adjustable Speed Drive Feeders.  Feeders 
to variable frequency drives, adjustable speed drives, and similar must be 
sized for voltage drop based on the drive’s maximum input current, 
including any drive losses.  Additionally, this circuit must be considered a 
“branch circuit” for voltage drop compliance purposes only. 
e. 
Other Feeders Directly Supplying Motor-Based Equipment.  Where 
NFPA 70 categorizes conductors as feeders, but the conductors supply 
dedicated motor-based equipment or equipment assemblies such as 
cranes and elevators, the voltage drop calculation load must be the total 
FLA.  Application-specific NFPA 70 demand factors may be applied to the 
loads when used for voltage drop calculations.  Additionally, this circuit 
must be considered a “branch circuit” for voltage drop compliance 
purposes only. 
3-2.7.4.3.3 
Branch Circuit Loads. 
a. 
Lighting Circuits.  Lighting circuits must utilize the total full load of all 
luminaire and non-luminaire devices connected.  Where the lighting circuit 
contains non-luminaire components such as room controllers or power 
packs, ensure such loads are captured. 
b. 
Receptacle Circuits.  Receptacle circuits (including circuits where a 
dedicated receptacle is provided for a single device, appliance, or 
equipment) must use 80% of the circuit’s capacity for voltage drop 
calculations.  
c. 
Systems Furniture Circuits.  Systems furniture circuits must use 80% of 
the circuit’s capacity for voltage drop calculations. 
d. 
Hard-Wired Appliance and Other Non-Receptacle Circuits.  Hard-
wired appliance and other non-receptacle circuits must utilize the total 
connected load on the circuit for voltage drop calculations. 
3-2.7.4.4 
Circuit Lengths. 
3-2.7.4.4.1 
Methods. 
See UFC 3-520-01 for routing estimation instructions, and utilize the applicable method 
as described and assigned below. 

=== UFC 3-501-01 p.40 ===
UFC 3-501-01 
27 November 2024 
 
 
28 
a. 
End-of-Line Method.  Loads on circuits must be at the end of the circuit 
for voltage drop calculations unless otherwise indicated below. 
b. 
Point-to-Point Method.  Calculate the load contributions to voltage drop 
as a function of the load experienced for a given portion of the circuit 
except as identified in the subsequent entries of this section.  That is, the 
entire load on the circuit is experienced to the first device, be it a load, 
splicing/junction point, etc.  Beyond that point, the load is diminished for 
the next series or parallel lengths, and only those loads contribute to the 
voltage dropped in the associated circuit length. 
The totality of the voltage dropped on any given path must be evaluated in 
determining a satisfactory conductor size (i.e., the path to one end device 
may experience less voltage drop than the path to a different end device), 
and the more severe condition in a comparison of multiple paths must be 
used for the entire circuit size. 
3-2.7.4.4.2 
Feeders. 
The entire feeder conductor lengths from the start of calculation described above to the 
last circuit breaker or fuse for a given portion of the distribution system must be used in 
the voltage drop calculation using the End-of-Line method. 
3-2.7.4.4.3 
Branch Circuits. 
As with feeder conductors, the entire length of the branch circuit conductors (End-of-
Line) must be used in the calculation except as follows for the purposes of the voltage 
drop load location: 
a. 
Lighting Circuits.  Lighting circuits may use the Point-to-Point Method. 
Where the lighting circuit contains non-luminaire components such as 
room controllers, power packs, or other line-voltage control devices, 
ensure the lengths used and loads associated used in the voltage drop 
calculation capture these portions of the circuit, including travelers 
between three- and four-way switches. 
b. 
Receptacle Circuits.  The load identified above must be at the farthest 
receptacle (End-of-Line) as routed through other receptacles, junction 
boxes, control devices, etc. 
c. 
Systems Furniture Circuits.  The load identified above must be at the 
point of connection to the assembly (End-of-Line) as routed through 
junction boxes, control devices, etc., prior to the point of systems furniture 
connection. 
d. 
Hard-Wired Appliances and Other Non-Receptacle Circuits.  Hard-
wired appliances and other non-receptacle circuits may use the Point-to-
Point Method. 

=== UFC 3-501-01 p.41 ===
UFC 3-501-01 
27 November 2024 
 
 
29 
3-2.7.4.5 
Additional Calculation Considerations. 
3-2.7.4.5.1 
Circuit Breakers in Series for Singular Loads or Set of Receptacles. 
In situations where a circuit supplies a singular load or set of receptacles but is provided 
with an additional overcurrent protective device local to the load, the two portions of the 
distribution system may collectively be considered as part of the “branch circuit” for 
voltage drop calculations.  For example, if an interior panelboard circuit breaker supplies 
an exterior pedestal-mounted receptacle with a local circuit breaker, the combined 
length of the circuits from the panelboard circuit breaker to the pedestal circuit breaker 
and from the pedestal circuit breaker to the receptacle may be sized using the branch 
circuit requirements for voltage drop (rather than the circuit from the panelboard circuit 
breaker to the pedestal circuit breaker being considered part of the feeder portion of the 
distribution system). 
3-2.7.4.5.2 
Branch Circuits Containing a Mix of Load Types. 
Use the worst-case load assignment for the voltage drop calculation.  Where portions of 
the circuit are distinguishable by load type, the worst-case voltage drop calculation may 
be performed for each full path from source to end device and the worst-case of the 
comparative results must be used. 
For example, a branch circuit is routed to a junction box, where the circuit is split into 
separate circuit paths (‘A’) for a set of receptacles and (‘B’) for a set of luminaires.  The 
entirety of the circuit load must be included from the source to the divergent point at the 
junction box; include the voltage drop to this point in the sizing for the comparative 
calculations.  Then use the sizing results from the comparative calculations between ‘A’ 
and ‘B’ to establish a circuit size. 
3-2.7.4.5.3 
Voltage Drop through Transformers. 
Voltage drop through transformers due to transformer losses for design calculation 
purposes must be zero.  When modeling, configure transformers such that the voltage 
drop percentages relative to the values identified in section “Initial Voltage” above on 
the transformer primary and secondary buses match.  That is, if the totality of the 
voltage dropped to the transformer primary terminations is, for example, 1.50% of the 
nominal system primary voltage, the calculation for the start of the conductors at the 
transformer secondary lugs must be at 1.50% of the nominal system secondary voltage.  
The aforementioned load associated with transformer losses are to be accounted for in 
the voltage drop calculations for the distribution system upstream of the transformer. 
Voltage drop mitigation measures must be through conductor size increases only, and 
through strategic selection of voltage systems and locations of transformation 
equipment. 
Transformer taps must not be used in voltage drop design calculations and must be 
used for field adjustments only, including to account for voltage lost through the 
transformer or longer conductor routing lengths than estimated in design.  Note the 

=== UFC 3-501-01 p.42 ===
UFC 3-501-01 
27 November 2024 
 
 
30 
output voltage of a transformer will drop as the load increases or the power factor 
decreases. 
3-2.7.4.5.4 
Voltage Drop Allowances Addressed by Industry Standards. 
For specific applications whereby a published industry standard establishes a voltage 
tolerance wider than the requirements of this section, the requirements of this section 
will end at the point at which the facility distribution system interfaces with the specific 
appliance, equipment, or similar system.  For example, the voltage drop limits provided 
by this section must be met for crane systems to the point of connection at the runway 
electrification system, however, the voltage drop experienced through the runway and 
subsequent conduction paths to the eventual loads may adhere to CMAA-70 instead. 
Similarly, the additional voltage drop experienced through appliance cord and plug 
connections are not covered under this section’s requirements, which end at the 
receptacle connection point.

Coordinate with the HVAC designer to determine expected maximum 
ambient temperatures in each building space, including ceiling cavities 
and plenums where conductors will be routed, perimeter walls, and the 
building exterior. Do not assume less than 78 degrees F (25 degrees C) 
for ambient temperature correction factors. 
Note: Recommend documenting these determinations graphically on a 
plan using the applicable temperature ranges for which adjustments are 
made in NFPA 70 Article 310 for graphical depiction. Require further 
adjustments to be made during construction based on the contractor 
exercising their routing discretion for routing not explicitly shown. Indicate 
on the contract documents the ambient temperature the design 
considered for sizing conductors and require further adjustments should 
the contractor's final routing path traverse an area of higher ambient 
temperature. 
Note: Circuits are typically sized individually and consolidation of circuits 
into a common raceway may occur during construction, requiring further 
adjustments to be made during construction based on the contractor 
exercising their discretion to consolidate multiple circuits into a common 
raceway for lengths exceeding the exception threshold for adjustments 
and corrections in NFPA 70. Indicate on the contract documents the 
number of conductors the design considered to be current carrying.  This 
information is useful when resizing conductors due to potential circuit 
consolidation. 
• 
For voltage drop requirements, see UFC 3-501-01.  
• 
For ambient temperature and voltage drop calculations, include 
anticipated routing of circuits in all directions (lateral and vertical). Unless 
explicitly identified to be installed in such a manner, do not assume 
underground routing will occur for conductor sizing factor purposes; 
overhead routing will typically require additional circuit lengths. Assume 
conduit routing at right angles to the building structure unless specifically 
shown on the plans; diagonal routing may be used for calculations only if 
indicated on the plans. 
Note: Routing concept adapted from the ASHRAE 90.1 User’s Manual. 
This estimate should account for any known conditions shown on the 
plans including room and structure geometry. 
• 
Where conductor size increases to mitigate voltage drop exceed the 
maximum permitted by a given device termination, the conductor size may 
be reduced to terminate properly in accordance with manufacturer 
requirements. Select splice kits, junctions, cable-reducing adapters, etc., 
to accommodate the increased wire size. Where a conductor size has 
been adjusted to mitigate voltage drop and conductor size reduction is 
required, the following restrictions will apply:

18 
• 
Validate that transformer size has not been increased by the 
design approach taken to comply with ASHRAE 90.1. 
Any design calculations exceeding these requirements must be specifically approved by 
the Technical Reviewing Authority. 
c. 
Load Analysis for Emergency/Standby Generator: 
• 
Provide sizing calculations including starting kVA. 
• 
Refer to UFC 3-540-01 for additional load analysis requirements, 
including the effect of UPS systems on generator sizing. 
d. 
Load Analysis for Alternate Energy Systems: 
• 
Provide maximum power calculations applicable to the type of

Load Analysis Criteria. 
Use the following additional criteria for the load analysis: 
• 
Assign a “0%” demand factor for fire pump loads in demand calculations. 
• 
Design underground service entrance distribution using commercially-
available thermal analysis software based on Neher-McGrath or finite 
element methods. Assume a load factor of 100%.

Size the service entrance conductors for a continuous load current not 
less than the ampacity of the main bus in the service entrance equipment. 
For example, provide conductors sized for 1200 amperes with 1200

Listed conductor size adapters are acceptable. Design main service 
equipment to provide a minimum of approximately 15% combination of

def get_conduit_size(n_ph, ph_od, egc_od, ref_rw):
    a_tot = n_ph * (math.pi / 4.0) * (ph_od ** 2) + (math.pi / 4.0) * (egc_od ** 2)
    for rw in sorted(conduit_data.keys()):
        if rw < ref_rw: continue

                if 2.8 <= jam <= 3.2:

            return rw
    return None

def rca_duct(De, tins, Did, Dod, Db, L):
    Dc = De - 2.0 * tins
    Ri = (rho_i / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(De / Dc)
    Rd = (rho_pvc / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(Dod / Did) + 0.40
    Re = (rho_e / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(4.0 * L / Dod)
    Rb = ((rho_c - rho_e) / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(4.0 * L / Db)
    return Ri + Rd + Re + Rb

def rac_90(rac75, alpha):
    return (rac75 / 304.8) * (1.0 + alpha * 70.0) / (1.0 + alpha * 55.0)

rac_f10 = rac_90(al_map["500 kcmil"][3], 0.00403)
W_se = 3.0 * ((1732.0 / 6.0) ** 2) * rac_se
W_f10 = 3.0 * ((432.0 / 2.0) ** 2) * rac_f10
occ_db1 = {d: W_se for d in se_ducts}
for d in f10_ducts: occ_db1[d] = W_f10
dtm_db1 = {}
for di, wi in occ_db1.items():
    xi, yi = db1_coords[di]
    dtm_db1[di] = sum(
        LF * wj * (rho_e / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(math.hypot(xi - db1_coords[dj][0], yi + db1_coords[dj][1]) / math.hypot(xi - db1_coords[dj][0], yi - db1_coords[dj][1]))
        for dj, wj in occ_db1.items() if dj != di
    )
Rca_se = rca_duct(0.849, 0.065, 5.047, 5.563, Db1, L1_center)
Rca_f10 = rca_duct(0.849, 0.065, 5.047, 5.563, Db1, L1_center)

        for dj in f05_ducts if dj != di

def tray_icorr(mat, sz):
    r = cu_map[sz] if mat == "CU" else al_map[sz]

    rac90 = rac_90(r[3], alpha)

    itherm = math.sqrt((90.0 - 46.0 - dTs_tray) / (rac90 * Rth * kt_tray))
    return min(float(r[10]), itherm)  # capped by 75 C free-air column per Section 5.5

        ccc = 3 if ph == 3 else 2

        # Find min_amp_sz for EGC scaling per Section 5.7
        min_amp_sz = None

            if ic * sets >= Ides - 1e-9:

        if mat == "CU" and sz == "12": icorr = min(icorr, 20.0)

        egc = b_egc
        rw = ""
        rw_str = ""
    else:

        rw = ""
        rw_str = ""
        if ckt == "SE-1":

        elif ckt == "F-10":

# Basis of Design — Low-Voltage Wire Schedule (Building 4210, Project P-4210)

## 1. Codes of Record, Adopting Criteria, and Order of Precedence

This wire schedule and calculation package for Building 4210 (Consolidated Support Facility) at Naval Support Activity Whitmore Ridge was prepared against the codes and standards in effect at the start of design (**14 July 2025**, per Sheet `G-001_code_of_record_and_general_notes.dxf` and `NSA-WR_EDS-26_electrical_design_standard_rev4.pdf` §1.1):

1. **Adopting Document:** **UFC 1-200-01** (*DoD Building Code*, 1 September 2022, Change 4 of 17 December 2024).
2. **Building Code of Record:** **IBC 2024 Edition** (*International Building Code*), adopted and modified by `UFC 1-200-01`.
3. **Electrical Code of Record:** **NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023 Edition** (*National Electrical Code*), adopted via `UFC 1-200-01` §1-6.2 and **UFC 3-501-01** (*Electrical Engineering*, 27 November 2024).
4. **Governing Federal Criteria:** **UFC 3-501-01** (27 November 2024), **UFC 3-520-01** (*Interior Electrical Systems*, 16 January 2025), and **UFC 1-200-02** (referencing ASHRAE 90.1).
5. **Installation Design Standard:** **NSA-WR EDS-26 Revision 4** (*Electrical Design Standard — Building Distribution*, 12 June 2026).
6. **Contract Specifications:** Section **26 05 19** (*Low-Voltage Electrical Power Conductors and Cables*, fixing **Cascadia Wire & Cable Section 4, Issue 2026-1** as the Basis of Design), Section **26 05 33** (*Raceways and Boxes for Electrical Systems*), and Section **26 24 16** (*Panelboards*).

**Order of Precedence & Document Resolution:** Per Sheet `G-001` and `NSA-WR EDS-26 Rev 4` §1.1, where two governing documents set different limits on the same quantity, **the more restrictive requirement governs**; where `EDS-26 Rev 4` is silent, the applicable UFC governs. Superseded or non-governing documents in the data room were explicitly excluded from governing decisions:
- `owner/NSA-WR_EDS-26_electrical_design_standard_rev2_SUPERSEDED.pdf` (superseded on 12 June 2026 by Revision 4).
- `drawings/E-601_one_line_REV_A_SUPERSEDED.pdf` (superseded by IFC drawing `E-601_one_line_diagram.dxf`).
- `vendor/Meridian_Cable_building_wire_datasheet.pdf` (not the Basis of Design under Specification `26_05_19_low_voltage_conductors.pdf` §1.3).
- `drawings/E-401_fire_alarm_riser.dxf` (power-limited fire alarm circuits excluded from scope per `E-401` note and `EDS-26 Rev 4` §1).

## 2. Environmental Parameters and Provenance

- **Outdoor Design Dry-Bulb (`outdoor_design_dry_bulb_c = 42 °C`):** From `site/NOAA_daily_normals_1991-2020_USW00003145.csv`, the highest daily normal maximum (`DLY-TMAX-NORMAL`) is `106.8 °F` (`41.556 °C`). Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.4, rounding up to the next whole degree Celsius gives **`42 °C`**.
- **Roof Cable Tray Ambient (`roof_ambient_c = 46 °C`) & Solar Irradiance (`solar_irradiance_w_m2 = 1030 W/m²`):** Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.4 and `site/M-501-C_ambient_temperature_coordination_memo.pdf` §3, unshaded roof ladder tray `CT-R1` has ambient `42 °C + 4 K = 46 °C`, solar irradiance `S = 1030 W/m²`, absorptivity `alpha_s = 0.6`, and convection coefficient `h = 14.0 W/(m²·K)` (`Delta_T_s = 14.05 K`).
- **Undisturbed Earth Ambient (`earth_ambient_c = 27.45 °C`):** Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.2, undisturbed earth ambient is the annual mean of `DLY-TAVG-NORMAL` (`76.004 °F = 24.446 °C`) plus `3 K` = **`27.45 °C`**. Spot temperature logger readings (`22.1–28.4 °C` in `GEO-4210-T_thermal_resistivity_report.pdf` §4) are rejected per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.2.
- **Soil and Concrete Thermal Resistivity (`0.60 K·m/W` and `0.55 K·m/W`):** Per `GEO-4210-T_thermal_resistivity_report.pdf` §3.1–3.2 and `E-619_duct_bank_sections.dxf`, `DB-1` and `DB-2` trenches are backfilled for their full width and depth with fluidised thermal backfill (`0.60 K·m/W`) around a 3000 psi concrete encasement (`0.55 K·m/W`). Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.3, the backfill resistivity (`0.60 K·m/W`) governs the earth and mutual-heating terms, and the native sandy clay resistivity (`0.95 K·m/W` in `GEO-4210-T` §2) is rejected.
- **Interior Space Ambient Temperatures (`40 °C` and `45 °C`):** Per `M-501-C` §2, circuits routed through Mechanical Room 104 (`F-01`, `B-11`..`B-15`) and Fire Pump Room 108 (`F-03`) are evaluated at **`45 °C`** ambient; all other interior raceway circuits are evaluated at **`40 °C`** ambient.

## 3. Voltage-Drop Budget Allocation, Starting Point, and Low-Voltage Transformer Rule

- **Starting Point (`vd_start_point`):** Per `site/WRPU_service_availability_letter.pdf` (`WRPU-2026-0412`, §2), Whitmore Ridge Public Utilities owns and maintains pad-mounted transformer `T-1` (`1500 kVA`), and government ownership begins at the secondary lugs of `T-1`. Per `UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.1 and `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.1, the secondary lugs of `T-1` are the starting point of the voltage-drop calculation (`SE-1` is the first segment).
- **Service-Entrance Voltage-Drop Load (`SE-1`):** Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §2.3, `UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.3.1 sets the voltage-drop load of a service entrance to 100% of the service device rating (**`1600 A`** on `MSB-1`), whereas §3-2.7.4.3.2 references the required bus ampacity (**`2000 A`**). This design adopts **`1600 A`** (`VD(SE-1) = 1.04%`, `drop_v = 5.01 V`). (Even at `2000 A`, `VD(SE-1) = 1.30%`, and every feeder chain remains `<= 3.04%`).
- **No Reset at Low-Voltage Transformer `K-13` (`transformer_reset = false`):** Per `UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.5.3 and `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.1, voltage-drop counts do **not** restart at low-voltage dry-type transformer `K-13` (`75 kVA`, `480V–208Y/120V`).
- **Branch Circuits Inheriting Upstream Budget (`18 branch/motor circuits total, including 10 downstream of LV transformer K-13`):**
  - **10 circuits on `LP-1` (`B-01` through `B-10`, downstream of `K-13`)** inherit the 4-link feeder chain `SE-1 (1.04%) + F-02 (0.36%) + F-06 (0.16%) + F-07 (1.20%) = 2.77% <= 3.0%`. To keep cumulative voltage drop `<= 5.0%` (`branch VD <= 2.23%`), `B-01`, `B-03`, `B-04`, `B-05`, `B-08` are sized at `#8 AWG CU` and `B-02`, `B-06`, `B-07` at `#6 AWG CU` (with proportional EGC scaling per `NFPA 70` 250.122(B)), giving a maximum cumulative voltage drop of **`4.86%`** (on `B-06` and `B-09`).
  - **3 circuits on `DP-3` (`B-16` through `B-18` in Building 4212)** inherit `SE-1 (1.04%) + F-05 (1.54%) = 2.58% <= 3.0%`. Because `CMP-1` (`B-17`) accepts at most a single `#6 AWG` conductor per terminal (`VD(B-17) = 2.35%`), `F-05` (`716 ft` in `DB-2`) is sized at `3 sets of 600 kcmil AL` (`VD = 1.54%`, `250 kcmil CU` EGC), limiting cumulative voltage drop at `CMP-1` (`B-17`) to **`4.93% <= 5.0%`**. Circuit `B-18` (`194 ft` lighting circuit) is upsized to `#8 AWG CU` (`VD = 1.97%`, `cum_vd = 4.55% <= 5.0%`).
  - **5 motor feeders on `MCC-1` (`B-11` through `B-15`)** inherit `SE-1 (1.04%) + F-01 (1.53%) = 2.58% <= 3.0%`, with maximum cumulative voltage drop of **`3.78% <= 5.0%`** (on `B-15`).
- **Equipment-Specific Limits (`F-03`, `F-09`, `F-11`):**
  - **Fire Pump (`F-03`, `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.6.3 & `NFPA 70` Art. 695):** With `#1 AWG CU`, running voltage drop is `0.30%` (`cumulative = 1.34% <= 5.0%`), and locked-rotor (`543 A` at `PF = 0.35`) drop is `1.01%` (`cumulative = 2.05% <= 15.0%`).
  - **Elevator (`F-11`, `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.6.2):** With `#3 AWG CU`, feeder own voltage drop is `1.16% <= 2.0%` (`cumulative = 2.21% <= 5.0%`).
  - **ASD/VFD (`F-09`, `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.6.4):** Reactance is multiplied by `1.25` (`X = 1.25 * 0.0375 = 0.0469 ohm/kft`), yielding `VD(F-09) = 1.00%` (`cumulative = 2.41% <= 5.0%`).

## 4. Service-Entrance Sizing Decision (`SE-1`)

# Build parent map automatically from `from` -> `to` in connected load schedule

Ta_e = (76.00355 - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0 + 3.0  # 27.4464 C
Tc = 90.0; rho_i = 3.5; rho_pvc = 6.0; rho_e = 0.60; rho_c = 0.55; LF = 1.0
db1_coords = {
    "D1": (6.3, 36.0), "D2": (15.3, 36.0), "D3": (24.3, 36.0), "D4": (33.3, 36.0),
    "D5": (6.3, 45.0), "D6": (15.3, 45.0), "D7": (24.3, 45.0), "D8": (33.3, 45.0),
    "D9": (6.3, 54.0), "D10": (15.3, 54.0)
}
Db1 = math.sqrt(4.0 / math.pi * 39.6 * 29.6)
L1_center = 30.0 + 29.6 / 2.0

db2_coords = {"E1": (5.75, 35.5), "E2": (13.75, 35.5), "E3": (5.75, 43.5)}
Db2 = math.sqrt(4.0 / math.pi * 19.5 * 19.5)
L2_center = 30.0 + 19.5 / 2.0

def rca_duct(De, tins, Did, Dod, Db, L):
    Dc = De - 2.0 * tins
    Ri = (rho_i / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(De / Dc)
    Rd = (rho_pvc / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(Dod / Did) + 0.40
    Re = (rho_e / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(4.0 * L / Dod)
    Rb = ((rho_c - rho_e) / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(4.0 * L / Db)
    return Ri + Rd + Re + Rb

def rac_90(rac75, alpha):
    return (rac75 / 304.8) * (1.0 + alpha * 70.0) / (1.0 + alpha * 55.0)

# DB-1 mutual heating and ampacities
se_ducts = opt_choices["SE-1"][3].split(",")
f10_ducts = opt_choices["F-10"][3].split(",")
rac_se = rac_90(cu_map["500 kcmil"][3], 0.00393)
rac_f10 = rac_90(al_map["500 kcmil"][3], 0.00403)
W_se = 3.0 * ((1732.0 / 6.0) ** 2) * rac_se
W_f10 = 3.0 * ((432.0 / 2.0) ** 2) * rac_f10
occ_db1 = {d: W_se for d in se_ducts}
for d in f10_ducts: occ_db1[d] = W_f10
dtm_db1 = {}
for di, wi in occ_db1.items():
    xi, yi = db1_coords[di]
    dtm_db1[di] = sum(
        LF * wj * (rho_e / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(math.hypot(xi - db1_coords[dj][0], yi + db1_coords[dj][1]) / math.hypot(xi - db1_coords[dj][0], yi - db1_coords[dj][1]))
        for dj, wj in occ_db1.items() if dj != di
    )

Rca_f10 = rca_duct(0.849, 0.065, 5.047, 5.563, Db1, L1_center)
icorr_se = min(float(cu_map["500 kcmil"][7]), math.sqrt((Tc - Ta_e - max(dtm_db1[d] for d in se_ducts)) / (3.0 * rac_se * Rca_se)))
icorr_f10 = min(float(al_map["500 kcmil"][7]), math.sqrt((Tc - Ta_e - max(dtm_db1[d] for d in f10_ducts)) / (3.0 * rac_f10 * Rca_f10)))

# DB-2 mutual heating and ampacity
f05_ducts = opt_choices["F-05"][3].split(",")
rac_f05 = rac_90(al_map["600 kcmil"][3], 0.00403)

dtm_db2 = {}
for di in f05_ducts:
    xi, yi = db2_coords[di]
    dtm_db2[di] = sum(
        LF * W_f05 * (rho_e / (2.0 * math.pi)) * math.log(math.hypot(xi - db2_coords[dj][0], yi + db2_coords[dj][1]) / math.hypot(xi - db2_coords[dj][0], yi - db2_coords[dj][1]))
        for dj in f05_ducts if dj != di
    )

icorr_f05 = min(float(al_map["600 kcmil"][7]), math.sqrt((Tc - Ta_e - max(dtm_db2.values())) / (3.0 * rac_f05 * Rca_f05)))

        egc = b_egc
        rw = ""

    else:

        ccc = 3
        rw = ""
        rw_str = ""
        if ckt == "SE-1":

## 3. Hard Constraints & Engineering Rules Not to Break
1. **Ampacity Basis (EDS-26 Rev 4 §5.1–5.5, Cascadia Wire §4):**
   - Raceway: 90 °C column × `sqrt((90 - Ta)/(90 - 30))` × `sqrt(3/N)`, capped at the unadjusted termination temperature column (`60 °C` for OCPD <= 100 A or 60 °C lug rating; `75 °C` for OCPD > 100 A with 75 °C lug rating).
   - Roof Cable Tray (`CT-R1`): Free-air heat balance `I = sqrt((Tc - Ta - dT_s)/(Rac(90°C) * Rth * k_t))` with `Ta = roof_ambient_c (46 °C)`, `S = 1030 W/m²`, `alpha_s = 0.6`, `h = 14.0 W/(m²·K)`, `k_t = 1 + 0.06*(N - 3)` where `N` is total current-carrying conductors in the tray, capped at the unadjusted 75 °C Free Air table column.
   - Duct Bank (`DB-1`, `DB-2`): Simplified Neher-McGrath per EDS-26 Rev 4 §5.3 with `LF = 1.0`, `rho_e = 0.60 K·m/W`, `rho_c = 0.55 K·m/W`, `Ta_e` from NOAA station normals mean + 3 K, mutual heating `W_j` from operating current (`I_conn / sets`) of all loaded ducts in the bank, capped at the unadjusted 75 °C Raceway table column.

   - Branch circuits (`B-01`..`B-07`, `B-09`, `B-10`, `B-16`, `B-18`): `max(1.25 * continuous_load + non_continuous_load, OCPD)`.
3. **Voltage Drop & Cumulative Budget (UFC 3-501-01 §3-2.7, EDS-26 Rev 4 §2.3, §4.6.3, §5.6):**
   - Start point: T-1 secondary lugs (point of government ownership).

   - Fire pump (`F-03`): <= 5% total running VD at FLA (`96 A`) and <= 15% total starting VD at LRA (`543 A`), including upstream `SE-1` drop.
4. **Physical, Termination, Standardization & Raceway Constraints (EDS-26 Rev 4 §3, §5.7, §6, UFC 3-520-01 §3-6.3.1):**
   - Minimum conductor `#12 AWG`; `#6 AWG` and smaller must be `CU`; `#4 AWG` and larger may be `AL` or `CU` (all EGC must be `CU`).
   - Parallel sets: only for `1/0 AWG` and larger, max 6 sets, cannot exceed equipment `terminals provided per phase`, conductor size cannot exceed `largest conductor accepted per terminal` (unless reduced at termination per UFC 3-520-01 §3-6.3.2, though direct compliance is preferred).
   - Standardization: at most **5 distinct phase-conductor sizes larger than #1 AWG** across the entire project.
   - EGC sized per NEC Table 250.122 and scaled proportionally by circular mils (`NEC 250.122(B)`) whenever the phase conductor is increased above the minimum admissible ampacity-compliant size on that circuit.
   - Conduit/duct fill <= 40% (for >= 3 conductors), no jam ratio in `[2.8, 3.2]` for 3 conductors, raceway size >= Cascadia reference trade size, and roof tray `sum(OD) <= 0.90 * 18 in = 16.2 in`.

# Basis of Design — Low-Voltage Wire Schedule (Building 4210, Project P-4210)

## 1. Codes of Record, Adopting Criteria, and Order of Precedence

This wire schedule and calculation package for Building 4210 (Consolidated Support Facility) at Naval Support Activity Whitmore Ridge was prepared against the codes and standards in effect at the start of design (**14 July 2025**, per Sheet `G-001_code_of_record_and_general_notes.dxf` and `NSA-WR_EDS-26_electrical_design_standard_rev4.pdf` §1.1):

1. **Adopting Document:** **UFC 1-200-01** (*DoD Building Code*, 1 September 2022, Change 4 of 17 December 2024).
2. **Building Code of Record:** **IBC 2024 Edition** (*International Building Code*), adopted and modified by `UFC 1-200-01`.
3. **Electrical Code of Record:** **NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023 Edition** (*National Electrical Code*), adopted via `UFC 1-200-01` §1-6.2 and **UFC 3-501-01** (*Electrical Engineering*, 27 November 2024).
4. **Governing Federal Criteria:** **UFC 3-501-01** (27 November 2024), **UFC 3-520-01** (*Interior Electrical Systems*, 16 January 2025), and **UFC 1-200-02** (referencing ASHRAE 90.1).
5. **Installation Design Standard:** **NSA-WR EDS-26 Revision 4** (*Electrical Design Standard — Building Distribution*, 12 June 2026).
6. **Contract Specifications:** Section **26 05 19** (*Low-Voltage Electrical Power Conductors and Cables*, fixing **Cascadia Wire & Cable Section 4, Issue 2026-1** as the Basis of Design), Section **26 05 33** (*Raceways and Boxes for Electrical Systems*), and Section **26 24 16** (*Panelboards*).

**Order of Precedence & Document Resolution:** Per Sheet `G-001` and `NSA-WR EDS-26 Rev 4` §1.1, where two governing documents set different limits on the same quantity, **the more restrictive requirement governs**; where `EDS-26 Rev 4` is silent, the applicable UFC governs. Superseded or non-governing documents in the data room were explicitly excluded from governing decisions:
- `owner/NSA-WR_EDS-26_electrical_design_standard_rev2_SUPERSEDED.pdf` (superseded on 12 June 2026 by Revision 4).
- `drawings/E-601_one_line_REV_A_SUPERSEDED.pdf` (superseded by IFC drawing `E-601_one_line_diagram.dxf`).
- `vendor/Meridian_Cable_building_wire_datasheet.pdf` (not the Basis of Design under Specification `26_05_19_low_voltage_conductors.pdf` §1.3).
- `drawings/E-401_fire_alarm_riser.dxf` (power-limited fire alarm circuits excluded from scope per `E-401` note and `EDS-26 Rev 4` §1).

---

## 2. Environmental Parameters and Provenance

- **Outdoor Design Dry-Bulb (`outdoor_design_dry_bulb_c = 42 °C`):** From `site/NOAA_daily_normals_1991-2020_USW00003145.csv`, the highest daily normal maximum (`DLY-TMAX-NORMAL`) is `106.8 °F` (`41.556 °C`). Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.4, rounding up to the next whole degree Celsius gives **`42 °C`**.
- **Roof Cable Tray Ambient (`roof_ambient_c = 46 °C`) & Solar Irradiance (`solar_irradiance_w_m2 = 1030 W/m²`):** Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.4 and `site/M-501-C_ambient_temperature_coordination_memo.pdf` §3, unshaded roof ladder tray `CT-R1` has ambient `42 °C + 4 K = 46 °C`, solar irradiance `S = 1030 W/m²`, absorptivity `alpha_s = 0.6`, and convection coefficient `h = 14.0 W/(m²·K)` (`Delta_T_s = 14.05 K`).
- **Undisturbed Earth Ambient (`earth_ambient_c = 27.45 °C`):** Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.2, undisturbed earth ambient is the annual mean of `DLY-TAVG-NORMAL` (`76.004 °F = 24.446 °C`) plus `3 K` = **`27.45 °C`**. Spot temperature logger readings (`22.1–28.4 °C` in `GEO-4210-T_thermal_resistivity_report.pdf` §4) are rejected per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.2.
- **Soil and Concrete Thermal Resistivity (`0.60 K·m/W` and `0.55 K·m/W`):** Per `GEO-4210-T_thermal_resistivity_report.pdf` §3.1–3.2 and `E-619_duct_bank_sections.dxf`, `DB-1` and `DB-2` trenches are backfilled for their full width and depth with fluidised thermal backfill (`0.60 K·m/W`) around a 3000 psi concrete encasement (`0.55 K·m/W`). Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.3, the backfill resistivity (`0.60 K·m/W`) governs the earth and mutual-heating terms, and the native sandy clay resistivity (`0.95 K·m/W` in `GEO-4210-T` §2) is rejected.
- **Interior Space Ambient Temperatures (`40 °C` and `45 °C`):** Per `M-501-C` §2, circuits routed through Mechanical Room 104 (`F-01`, `B-11`..`B-15`) and Fire Pump Room 108 (`F-03`) are evaluated at **`45 °C`** ambient; all other interior raceway circuits are evaluated at **`40 °C`** ambient.

---

## 3. Voltage-Drop Budget Allocation, Starting Point, and Low-Voltage Transformer Rule

- **Starting Point (`vd_start_point`):** Per `site/WRPU_service_availability_letter.pdf` (`WRPU-2026-0412`, §2), Whitmore Ridge Public Utilities owns and maintains pad-mounted transformer `T-1` (`1500 kVA`), and government ownership begins at the secondary lugs of `T-1`. Per `UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.1 and `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.1, the secondary lugs of `T-1` are the starting point of the voltage-drop calculation (`SE-1` is the first segment).
- **Service-Entrance Voltage-Drop Load (`SE-1`):** Per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §2.3, `UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.3.1 sets the voltage-drop load of a service entrance to 100% of the service device rating (**`1600 A`** on `MSB-1`), whereas §3-2.7.4.3.2 references the required bus ampacity (**`2000 A`**). This design adopts **`1600 A`** (`VD(SE-1) = 1.04%`, `drop_v = 5.01 V`). (Even at `2000 A`, `VD(SE-1) = 1.30%`, and every feeder chain remains `<= 3.04%`).
- **No Reset at Low-Voltage Transformer `K-13` (`transformer_reset = false`):** Per `UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.5.3 and `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.1, voltage-drop counts do **not** restart at low-voltage dry-type transformer `K-13` (`75 kVA`, `480V–208Y/120V`).
- **Branch Circuits Inheriting Upstream Budget (`18 branch/motor circuits total, including 10 downstream of LV transformer K-13`):**
  - **10 circuits on `LP-1` (`B-01` through `B-10`, downstream of `K-13`)** inherit the 4-link feeder chain `SE-1 (1.04%) + F-02 (0.36%) + F-06 (0.16%) + F-07 (1.20%) = 2.77% <= 3.0%`. To keep cumulative voltage drop `<= 5.0%` (`branch VD <= 2.23%`), `B-01`, `B-03`, `B-04`, `B-05`, `B-08` are sized at `#8 AWG CU` and `B-02`, `B-06`, `B-07` at `#6 AWG CU` (with proportional EGC scaling per `NFPA 70` 250.122(B)), giving a maximum cumulative voltage drop of **`4.86%`** (on `B-06` and `B-09`).
  - **3 circuits on `DP-3` (`B-16` through `B-18` in Building 4212)** inherit `SE-1 (1.04%) + F-05 (1.54%) = 2.58% <= 3.0%`. Because `CMP-1` (`B-17`) accepts at most a single `#6 AWG` conductor per terminal (`VD(B-17) = 2.35%`), `F-05` (`716 ft` in `DB-2`) is sized at `3 sets of 600 kcmil AL` (`VD = 1.54%`, `250 kcmil CU` EGC), limiting cumulative voltage drop at `CMP-1` (`B-17`) to **`4.93% <= 5.0%`**. Circuit `B-18` (`194 ft` lighting circuit) is upsized to `#8 AWG CU` (`VD = 1.97%`, `cum_vd = 4.55% <= 5.0%`).
  - **5 motor feeders on `MCC-1` (`B-11` through `B-15`)** inherit `SE-1 (1.04%) + F-01 (1.53%) = 2.58% <= 3.0%`, with maximum cumulative voltage drop of **`3.77% <= 5.0%`** (on `B-15`).
- **Equipment-Specific Limits (`F-03`, `F-09`, `F-11`):**
  - **Fire Pump (`F-03`, `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.6.3 & `NFPA 70` Art. 695):** With `#1 AWG CU`, running voltage drop is `0.30%` (`cumulative = 1.34% <= 5.0%`), and locked-rotor (`543 A` at `PF = 0.35`) drop is `1.01%` (`cumulative = 2.05% <= 15.0%`).
  - **Elevator (`F-11`, `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.6.2):** With `#3 AWG CU`, feeder own voltage drop is `1.16% <= 2.0%` (`cumulative = 2.21% <= 5.0%`).
  - **ASD/VFD (`F-09`, `EDS-26 Rev 4` §4.6.4):** Reactance is multiplied by `1.25` (`X = 1.25 * 0.0375 = 0.0469 ohm/kft`), yielding `VD(F-09) = 1.00%` (`cumulative = 2.41% <= 5.0%`).

---

## 4. Service-Entrance Sizing Decision (`SE-1`)

Although `MSB-1` has a `1600 A` main breaker, its bus ampacity is **`2000 A`** (`P-4210_equipment_schedule.xlsx` and `E-601_one_line_diagram.dxf`). Under **UFC 3-501-01 §3-2.3.3** and **EDS-26 Rev 4 §2.2**, low-voltage service-entrance conductors must be sized for **100% of the service switchboard bus rating (`2000 A`)**. Thus `SE-1` is sized for `design_current_a = 2000 A` using **6 parallel sets of `500 kcmil CU`** (`348.11 A/set * 6 = 2088.66 A >= 2000 A`) with a **`4/0 AWG CU`** EGC per duct (`EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.7, `NFPA 70` Table 250.122 for `1600 A` main device).

---

## 5. Underground Duct-Bank Assignment and Mutual-Heating Consequence

- **Service Duct Bank `DB-1` (`10 of 12 ducts available`):** Sheet `E-619_duct_bank_sections.dxf` shows `DB-1` as a `3 rows x 4 columns` (`12-duct`) concrete-encased `5 in EPC-40` bank (`9 in` horizontal/vertical center-to-center spacing, `30 in` cover to top of encasement, `39.6 in x 29.6 in` concrete envelope). Per `E-619`, **`D11` (spare - owner reserve) and `D12` (existing site lighting feeder) are reserved**, leaving **10 ducts (`D1` through `D10`)** available.
- **Thermal Assignment in `DB-1` (`mutual_heating_rise_k = 31.09 K`):**
  - `SE-1` (`6 sets of 500 kcmil CU`, operating current `1732 / 6 = 288.67 A/set`, `W_j = 25.00 W/m`): assigned to columns 1 and 2 (`D1, D2, D5, D6, D9, D10`).
  - `F-10` (`2 sets of 500 kcmil AL`, operating current `432 / 2 = 216.00 A/set`, `W_j = 23.03 W/m`): assigned to column 4 (`D4, D8`), leaving column 3 (`D3, D7`) empty as a thermal buffer.
  - Under the Neher-McGrath formulation in `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3 (`T_a,e = 27.45 °C`, `T_c = 90 °C`, `rho_e = 0.60 K·m/W`, `rho_c = 0.55 K·m/W`, `LF = 1.0`), the worst-case mutual-heating rise in `DB-1` is **`31.09 K`** (at interior duct `D5` of `SE-1`), yielding `corrected_ampacity_a = 348.11 A/set` on `SE-1` (`6 * 348.11 = 2088.66 A >= 2000 A`). On `F-10` (`D4, D8`), mutual heating from `SE-1` produces **`23.53 K`** (at `D8`), yielding `corrected_ampacity_a = 302.25 A/set` (`2 * 302.25 = 604.50 A >= 600 A`).
- **Duct Bank `DB-2` (`F-05` in `E1, E2, E3`):** Sheet `E-619` shows `DB-2` as a `2x2` (`4-duct`) `4 in EPC-40` bank (`8 in` spacing, `19.5 in x 19.5 in` envelope) with **`E4` reserved for communications**, leaving **3 ducts (`E1, E2, E3`)** available. `F-05` (`3 sets of 600 kcmil AL`, operating current `281 / 3 = 93.67 A/set`) occupies **`E1, E2, E3`**, experiencing `Delta_T_m = 1.54 K` (`i_therm = 399.65 A/set`), capped by the `75 °C` termination limit at **`336.00 A/set`**.

---

## 6. Roof Cable Tray, Material, Termination Rating, and Standardisation Decisions

- **Roof Ladder Tray `CT-R1` (`tray_sum_od_in = 12.206 in`, `ccc = 18`):** All four rooftop HVAC feeders (`F-04` and `F-12` at `2 sets of 4/0 AL` each; `F-08` and `F-13` at `1 set of 4/0 AL` each) share `CT-R1` (`6 sets = 18` current-carrying conductors total, `k_t = 1 + 0.06*(18 - 3) = 1.90`, `corrected_ampacity_a = 171.93 A/set`). The sum of all 24 cable ODs (18 phase + 6 EGC) is **`12.206 in <= 16.20 in`** (`90%` of the `18 in` usable tray width per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §6.3.2 and `26_05_33` §2.3).
- **Termination Temperature Limit (`EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.5 & `UFC 3-520-01` §3-6.3.1):** Every circuit with `ocpd_a <= 100 A` (`B-01`..`B-10`, `B-13`..`B-18`) as well as `F-07` (connected to `LP-1` with listed `60 °C` lugs) is capped by the `60 °C` ampacity column; circuits with `ocpd_a > 100 A` and `75 °C` lugs are capped by the `75 °C` column.
- **Standardisation (`distinct_large_sizes = 5`):** Across the entire project, exactly **5 distinct phase-conductor sizes larger than `#1 AWG`** are used (`4/0`, `300 kcmil`, `400 kcmil`, `500 kcmil`, `600 kcmil`), satisfying `EDS-26 Rev 4` §3.4.2 (`<= 5` sizes).

---

python3 -c "
import csv, math

with open('/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/wire_schedule.csv') as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))

print('Row count:', len(rows))
expected_cols = ['circuit', 'description', 'from', 'to', 'install_class', 'length_ft', 'sets', 'size', 'material', 'egc_size', 'raceway_trade_in', 'duct_ids', 'design_current_a', 'corrected_ampacity_a', 'vd_load_a', 'vd_pct', 'cumulative_vd_pct', 'ambient_c', 'ccc', 'governing_constraint', 'ocpd_a', 'system_voltage_v', 'phases', 'power_factor', 'r_ohm_per_kft', 'x_ohm_per_kft', 'drop_v']
assert list(rows[0].keys()) == expected_cols, 'Column mismatch!'

for r in rows:
    ckt = r['circuit']
    sets = int(r['sets'])
    i_des = float(r['design_current_a'])
    i_corr = float(r['corrected_ampacity_a'])
    assert sets * i_corr + 1e-6 >= i_des, f'{ckt}: sets*i_corr={sets*i_corr} < {i_des}'
    L = float(r['length_ft'])
    I_vd = float(r['vd_load_a'])
    V = float(r['system_voltage_v'])
    ph = int(r['phases'])
    pf = float(r['power_factor'])
    R = float(r['r_ohm_per_kft'])
    X = float(r['x_ohm_per_kft'])
    mult = math.sqrt(3) if ph == 3 else 2.0
    sin_phi = math.sqrt(max(0.0, 1.0 - pf**2))
    dv = mult * I_vd * (L / 1000.0) * (R * pf + X * sin_phi) / sets
    vdp = 100.0 * dv / V
    assert abs(dv - float(r['drop_v'])) <= 0.02, f'{ckt}: dv {dv} vs {r[\"drop_v\"]}'
    assert abs(vdp - float(r['vd_pct'])) <= 0.02, f'{ckt}: vdp {vdp} vs {r[\"vd_pct\"]}'
    assert float(r['cumulative_vd_pct']) <= 5.0, f'{ckt}: cum_vd {r[\"cumulative_vd_pct\"]} > 5.0'
    if ckt.startswith('B-'):
        assert float(r['vd_pct']) <= 3.0, f'{ckt}: branch vd {r[\"vd_pct\"]} > 3.0'

print('All 32 circuit mathematical and constraint assertions PASSED!')
"

steps.message:
The low-voltage wire schedule and supporting engineering package for **Building 4210, Consolidated Support Facility (Project P-4210)** at Naval Support Activity Whitmore Ridge have been completed and packaged in `/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/submission.zip`.

### Delivered Files (Top-Level in `/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/submission.zip`)
1. `wire_schedule.csv` (`/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/wire_schedule.csv`) — 32-circuit schedule (`B-01` through `B-18`, `F-01` through `F-13`, and `SE-1`) with all 27 required columns.
2. `E-621_wire_schedule.dxf` (`/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/E-621_wire_schedule.dxf`) — Contract drawing Sheet E-621 with project title block (`P-4210`), abbreviation legend, and `TEXT` entities for all 32 circuits matching `wire_schedule.csv`.
3. `calc_book.xlsx` (`/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/calc_book.xlsx`) — Calculation workbook containing `front_sheet`, `duct_assignment`, and `cost_ledger` with stored numerical values.
4. `design_basis.md` (`/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/design_basis.md`) — Engineering Basis of Design opening with the required structured `json` block followed by the narrative.
5. `constraint_register.xlsx` (`/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/constraint_register.xlsx`) — Code-compliance matrix registering 54 atomic requirements traced to governing clauses and explicitly documenting non-governing/superseded documents.

---

### Key Engineering Results
- **Codes of Record & Precedence:** **NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023 Edition** and **IBC 2024 Edition**, adopted by **UFC 1-200-01** (Change 4, 17 December 2024) as fixed at design start (14 July 2025), alongside **UFC 3-501-01** (27 November 2024), **UFC 3-520-01** (16 January 2025), and **NSA-WR EDS-26 Rev 4** (12 June 2026). Where criteria differ, the **most restrictive requirement governs** (`EDS-26 Rev 4` §1.1); superseded documents (`EDS-26 Rev 2`, `E-601 Rev A`), non-governing vendor data (`Meridian Cable`), and power-limited fire alarm circuits (`Sheet E-401`) do not govern.
- **Environmental & Thermal Parameters (`NFPA 70` §310.14(B) Neher-McGrath):**
  - Outdoor design dry-bulb: **`42 °C`** (`NOAA USW00003145` maximum `DLY-TMAX-NORMAL = 106.8 °F = 41.56 °C` rounded up per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.4).
  - Unshaded roof cable tray `CT-R1`: **`46 °C`** ambient (`42 °C + 4 K`), solar irradiance **`1030 W/m²`** (`absorptivity = 0.6`, `h = 14.0 W/(m²·K)`, `Delta_T_s = 14.05 K`), `18` current-carrying conductors (`k_t = 1.90`), total cable OD sum **`12.206 in <= 16.20 in`** (`90%` of `18 in` usable width).
  - Undisturbed earth ambient: **`27.45 °C`** (annual mean `DLY-TAVG-NORMAL = 76.00 °F = 24.45 °C + 3 K`; spot logger `22.1–28.4 °C` rejected per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.2).
  - Thermal resistivities: **`0.60 K·m/W`** fluidised thermal backfill (full trench width/depth; native sandy clay `0.95 K·m/W` rejected per `EDS-26 Rev 4` §5.3.3) and **`0.55 K·m/W`** concrete encasement at **`LF = 1.0`**.
  - Interior raceways: **`45 °C`** in Mechanical Room 104 (`F-01`, `B-11`..`B-15`) and Fire Pump Room 108 (`F-03`); **`40 °C`** in all other interior spaces (`M-501-C`).
- **Duct-Bank Assignment & Mutual Heating:**
  - `DB-1` (`10` ducts `D1..D10` available; `D11` owner spare and `D12` existing site lighting reserved per `E-619`): `SE-1` (`6 sets of 500 kcmil CU`, `4/0 CU` EGC) occupies **`D1, D2, D5, D6, D9, D10`** (`worst-case Delta_T_m = 31.09 K` at `D5`, `348.11 A/set`, `2088.66 A >= 2000 A` `MSB-1` bus rating); `F-10` (`2 sets of 500 kcmil AL`, `#1 CU` EGC) occupies **`D4, D8`** (`Delta_T_m = 23.53 K` at `D8`, `302.25 A/set`, `604.50 A >= 600 A`).
  - `DB-2` (`3` ducts `E1..E3` available; `E4` reserved for communications): `F-05` (`3 sets of 600 kcmil AL`, `250 kcmil CU` EGC) occupies **`E1, E2, E3`** (`Delta_T_m = 1.54 K`, capped at `336.00 A/set` by `75 °C` termination limit).
- **Voltage-Drop Allocation:** Starts at **`T-1` secondary lugs** (`WRPU-2026-0412`) and does **not** reset at low-voltage transformer `K-13` (`UFC 3-501-01` §3-2.7.4.5.3). Feeder-chain cumulative drops are **`1.04%`** at `MSB-1`, **`1.41%`** at `DP-2`, **`1.57%`** at `K-13`, **`2.58%`** at `MCC-1`, **`2.58%`** at `DP-3`, **`2.77%`** at `LP-1`, and **`2.78%`** at `ATS-1` (all `<= 3.0%`). All 18 branch/motor circuits satisfy `<= 3.0%` individual drop and `<= 5.0%` cumulative drop (maximum **`4.93%`** on `B-17`), and special equipment limits on `F-03` (`1.34%` running, `2.05%` locked rotor), `F-09` (`1.25x` reactance, `2.41%` cumulative), and `F-11` (`1.16% <= 2.0%` feeder) are met.
- **Standardisation & Installed Cost:** Uses exactly **5 distinct phase-conductor sizes larger than `#1 AWG`** (`4/0`, `300 kcmil`, `400 kcmil`, `500 kcmil`, `600 kcmil`). Total conductor length is **`40,888 ft`** (`>= 38,000 ft`), qualifying for the `-6%` campus quantity break:
  - **Conductors (net of `-6%` break):** `$70,387.43` material + `$22,996.99` labour = **`$93,384.42`**
  - **Terminations (`90 set-ends`):** `$5,105.26` material + `$4,504.06` labour = **`$9,609.32`**
  - **Interior Raceway (`4,257 ft` RMC):** `$21,406.08` material + `$26,183.52` labour = **`$47,589.60`**
  - **Total Installed Package Cost (`total_usd`):** `$96,898.77` material + `$53,684.57` labour = **`$150,583.34`**
